newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister says Kurd's north Iraq camp to close.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister says Kurd's north Iraq camp to close.

text.p: Turkey's defence minister said on Friday a Turkish Kurd refugee camp in northern Iraq would be closed because it shelters rebel Kurds who seek self-rule in southeastern Turkey.
"The Atrush camp will certainly be dispersed. The camp is totally a nest of terror now," Anatolian news agency quoted Defence Minister Turhan Tayan agency as saying.
The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR withdrew from Atrush in January, saying Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas were blocking its operations there.
But up to 14,000 people who fled the Kurdish conflict in southeast Turkey in 1994 are still living at the camp in tents and makeshift huts.
The UNHCR says only about 350 camp residents have resettled in Turkey in recent months despite Ankara calling for mass repatriation and guaranteeing security, housing and health care for returnees.
"The PKK terror organisation, which is trying to resist in Atrush camp, will be thrown out. We have an agreement with the United Nations. The United Nations will do what is necessary," Tayan said.
A UNHCR official in Ankara said the refugee agency had agreed to help any camp residents return to Turkey if they wanted. "That is the agreement we have. There is no new agreement," she said.
Many Atrush residents say they fled Turkey under pressure from the security forces but Ankara says the guerrillas forced them over the border to Iraqi Kurdish territory.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the 12-year conflict in southeast Turkey.
